input: In terms of programme, it is important to note that a significant budget overrun has been identified, and the forecast completion date has moved by a total of 6 weeks. This overrun has arisen because remeasurement of the installed quantities has increased the EPC forecast for the remaining civil and piping works, including work packages that were previously reported as complete. In other words, the work itself has been carried out, but the quantities involved are larger than those originally allowed for, and the remaining programme has therefore had to be extended. In order to address this issue, it is proposed that a single re-plan of the remaining work packages be undertaken, which will allow the unaffected packages to proceed in parallel with the remeasured work rather than in sequence. The project board will own this mitigation, approving the re-planned programme and reviewing progress against it at each status meeting. While the re-plan is expected to recover part of the lost time, it should be noted that the recovery will be partial, since some of the packages share the same supervision resources.
target:
The overrun stands at 6 weeks. Remeasurement of the installed quantities has raised the EPC forecast for the remaining civil and piping work, and the increase falls in packages that were reported complete at the last status point; the work is done, but the measured quantities exceed the quantities the forecast was built on, and the remaining programme lengthens accordingly. The forecast is restated on the remeasured quantities from this report onward. Two packages are unaffected, and their dates hold.

The mitigation is a single re-plan of the remaining packages, which compresses the sequence by running the unaffected packages in parallel with the remeasured work instead of after it. The project board owns the mitigation: the board approves the re-planned programme and takes the report against it at each status meeting. The re-plan recovers part of the lost time only where the parallel work does not compete for the same crews, and the civil packages share supervision with the remeasured work; the recovery is therefore partial, and the completion date moves by the unrecovered balance unless the board authorises additional resources.
